_readme: The SHARED corpus behind the DeviceShapes lockstep. `static/.../device-shapes.js` (typeFor)
and `netbox_facilitymap/device_shapes.py` (type_for) are a hand-maintained 1:1 mirror — there
is no build step, so the classification rules are duplicated, not shared. This file is the one
set of cases BOTH sides are driven through:
so a rule edited on one side and forgotten on the other fails on whichever side drifted,
instead of only ever being checked from Python.
Cases are stated in a SHAPE-NEUTRAL way, because the two ports take different item shapes:
the JS reads `item.role.slug`/`item.role.name`/`item.name`, Python reads flat `role_slug`/
`role_name`/`name`. Each side adapts these fields into its own shape. Fields are optional;
omitted ones are absent on both sides. `kind` defaults to 'device'.
Scope: the BUILT-IN English rules and the normalizer. The operator's `role_glyphs` vocabulary
needs per-test config on both sides and stays in each side's own tests.
`box` cases pin the per-type footprints, the other half of the lockstep.
